# Small-model llama.cpp inference in ET SysEmu

Run from this repository:

```sh
python3 examples/llama.py --model gpt2 --tokens 4 --layers 1
```

This downloads a pinned, SHA-256-checked GPT-2 small Q4_0 model, builds a
small C++ runner against the existing llama.cpp libraries, runs a CPU
control, and executes the same prompt through the ET SysEmu backend.
The default puts the last transformer layer on ET and keeps the tied
embedding/output weights on CPU. Increase `--layers` to place more
transformer layers on ET. `--device-output` also allows the output weights
on ET; the output layer counts as one additional layer.

For a much smaller model:

```sh
python3 examples/llama.py --model stories260k --tokens 2 --layers 5 --device-output
```

The TinyStories file is only 1,185,376 bytes. Its name is `stories260K`,
and llama.cpp reports 292,800 parameters and five transformer layers.
It is a Llama architecture model from the upstream test-model collection,
with limited language quality. GPT-2 is the actual GPT-2 architecture and
has 12 transformer layers; the Q4_0 file is 106,554,880 bytes.
GPT-2 small is conventionally a 124M-parameter model with tied weights;
this llama.cpp loader counts the duplicated output tensor and reports
163,037,184 parameters. Both counts refer to the same loaded model.
Neither model is a chat assistant. The runner performs greedy generation
with the original distribution and stops at EOS when the model emits it.

## CH1 Minion FPGA backend

The normal upstream `llama-cli` can load the same external backend through
`GGML_BACKEND_PATH`; a llama.cpp source patch is not required. Build against
the exact llama.cpp revision and libraries used by the CLI:

```sh
python3 fpga/tools/build_etminion_ggml_backend.py \
  --llama-dir "$LLAMA_SRC" --llama-build-dir "$LLAMA_BUILD" \
  --out-dir out/llama-cli-plugin-new

mkdir -p out/llama-cli-control
cat > out/llama-cli-control/raw.jinja <<'JINJA'
{{ bos_token }}{% for message in messages %}{{ message.content }}{% endfor %}
JINJA

GGML_BACKEND_PATH="$PWD/out/llama-cli-plugin-new/libggml-et-minion.so" \
GGML_ETFPGA_SOCKET=/tmp/etsoc-minion.sock \
ETFPGA_BUILD_ID=0x89a08cefe8470928 \
LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$LLAMA_BUILD/bin${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:+:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH}" \
  "$LLAMA_BUILD/bin/llama-cli" \
  -m out/llama/models/stories260K.gguf --device ET-Minion-CH1 -ngl 99 \
  -p 'Hello my name is' -n 2 --temp 0 --seed 1 \
  -c 128 -b 16 -ub 16 -t 2 --simple-io --no-display-prompt \
  --chat-template-file out/llama-cli-control/raw.jinja \
  --single-turn --no-warmup --flash-attn off --no-op-offload --no-kv-offload
```

Set `LLAMA_SRC` to the pinned llama.cpp checkout and `LLAMA_BUILD` to its
existing build directory. The service below must already be running against

# llama.cpp FPGA bring-up with CH1 only

Target: YPCB XC7K480T-FFG1156-2, complete eight-lane Minion, physical DRAM
CH1 only, 2 GiB usable memory. Work began October 18, 2026.

The current guest keeps instructions, parameters, environment and the C stack
in the original BRAM windows. Tensor payloads reside in CH1 DDR. The qualifier
also initializes a 64 KiB DDR region for additional memory coverage.

## Verified result — October 20

Physical TinyStories llama.cpp inference passes using the checked live JTAG
Minion service. Both tokens `[410, 454]` match CPU and retained SysEmu. All
512 logits at each of two steps are finite; maximum absolute FPGA/CPU
difference is `0.00011140108108520508`. All five transformer layers' supported
matrix operations and the output projection use the FPGA backend, with
62 actual dispatches and 5,811,064 retired Minion instructions. Attention and
unsupported operations/shapes use CPU.

Generation takes 104.997 s versus 476.169 s in the matching saved SysEmu test:
4.54× observed generation speedup. JTAG model-weight loading takes 261.209 s;
native CPU generation takes 0.016 s. The execution-cycle counter includes
completion-marker polling, so it is not a pure matrix-compute measurement.

All four current C kernel formats pass complete physical qualification. The
new [standalone basic-op examples](../../examples/fpga/README.md) also pass
22 physical cases across seven programs and all elementwise modes. The
hardware service and example tests have exited and released JTAG. Permanent
flash was not written.

Evidence: [inference result](../../out/llama-fpga/stories260k-20261020T180338-783e9b/result.json),
